Phase 24 moves trusted stale-decision pruning into an explicit administrator writer that revalidates snapshot trust and reports before/after counts; entity-detail GET now preserves decisions. Phase 25 adds an entity-drawer operator action that is hidden without GET eligibility, requires explicit browser confirmation, posts only to the existing prune route, refreshes decision/readiness state, and records the exact outcome. Phase 26 exercises that registered route: a subscriber receives rest_forbidden with no option mutation, while an administrator receives the exact pruned entity/proposal summaries. Phase 27 adds cache no-store to Proposal Review GET requests after the authenticated browser still showed a completely removed fixture; reloading returned zero fixture rows and zero prune actions, proving the residual display was stale client/browser state rather than persisted DBVC data. Phase 28 replaces the native prompt with an in-app modal; authenticated fixture QA verifies its exact copy, Cancel, no-op, and stale-prune paths. Phase 29 invalidates only an open fixture snapshot before confirmation; the authenticated drawer visibly renders the returned 409 text while both stored decisions remain intact. Phase 30 verifies the persistent accessible success status after an authoritative prune refresh, including exact removed/current counts, an empty selection state, and the absent action. Phase 31 finds the modal focus defect; Phase 32 then focuses Cancel on open and restores the prune opener after Escape, Cancel, and the modal Close control without mutating decisions. Phase 33 verifies closing the entity drawer restores the exact originating entity-row control without opening the prune confirmation or changing decisions. The fixture was removed completely. Decision, hash, status, recapture, and other write routes were not executed live, so the grouped record remains repository-tested rather than runtime verified.
